hints.title: Audit each equivalence
hints.body: Work through the lines and ask whether each new condition is equivalent to the previous one on the allowed domain.
hints.recap: The first unsupported line is the one where a valid implication or equivalence stops being justified.
hints.pitfall: A condition may be redundant rather than forgotten.
hints.pause: Identify any restriction apparently removed and check whether it imposed anything.

hints.title: Use the range of a square
hints.body: Find the smallest possible value of the expression between the two bounds after the square is removed.
hints.recap: For real inputs a squared expression is nonnegative; completing a square reveals a lower bound.
hints.pitfall: Check strict endpoints instead of relying only on a sketch.
hints.pause: Compare that range with the stated lower bound, then finish checking the remaining lines.

recall.reminder: For real inputs a squared expression is nonnegative; completing a square reveals a lower bound.

solution:
Adding 4 and factoring gives (x2−1)2<4. This is equivalent to −2<x2−1<2.

The lower inequality holds for every real x, since x2−1≥−1>−2. It can therefore be omitted without losing a restriction.

The upper inequality is x2<3, equivalent to −3<x<3. Every displayed step is valid. Answer A.
knowledgePattern: Check whether a discarded square-bound condition is automatic on the real domain
